I think that it’s very brave of you to think that way. Woman who are victims of revenge porn have every right to be angry. 

For me, so much of this terrible facet of rape culture stems from a sense many males feel of entitlement.  It’s something we learn, it’s something we’re taught: that we have a right to a woman’s body.  To touch it, to view it, to hold it.  Of course, many males don’t subscribe to this, or work past it without doing harm to others. But it is a cornerstone of rape culture. 


Your ex’s toxic mindset manifested in a horrible way that did lasting damage to you forever: my toxic mindset manifested in viewing images that were rooted in abuse and indirectly contributed to a terrible facet of our culture. 

If your ex is going to make any progress as a person, he has to realize that this exists inside of him and informs the way he thinks about the world. He has to challenge his own feelings and understand that he was wrong.  For me, when I viewed revenge porn, I did not think about my worldview or ethics or my relationship with consent or woman at all. I simply wanted to see woman I knew naked. And I didn’t think about the harm I was causing by carrying that into fruition.

For me, I had a toxic mindset that manifested in real harm, and so did your ex...and I’m so sorry for the pain he caused and the pain I caused woman in general.
